examples.en: Please mix lowercase letters and numbers in your password.

examples.ko: 이 칸에는 소문자만 입력할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only enter lowercase letters in this box.
Please write in lowercase, not capitals.
Lowercase letters are smaller than capital letters.
a is a lowercase letter and A is a capital letter.
The message my friend sent is all in lowercase.

explain: 반대말은 '대문자'예요. 영어에서는 문장의 첫 글자와 이름을 대문자로 쓰고, 나머지는 보통 소문자로 써요. 한글에는 대문자와 소문자 구분이 없어서 영어 같은 알파벳 글자를 이야기할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is 대문자 (uppercase). In English you capitalize the first letter of a sentence and names, and write the rest in lowercase. Hangul has no uppercase/lowercase distinction, so this word is used when talking about the English alphabet and other Latin letters.

examples.en: People gathered at the venue from the morning.
We took a bus to the venue.
The venue was so big that I got lost.
After the match we took photos at the venue.
The players cleaned the venue and went home.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 대회장으로 가는 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: It rained, so the road to the venue was jammed.

explain: '경기장'은 운동 경기를 하는 곳이고, '대회장'은 대회가 열리는 장소 전체를 가리켜요. 그래서 노래 대회나 요리 대회가 열리는 곳도 '대회장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 경기장 is the place where a sports match is played, while 대회장 is the whole place where a contest or event is held. So the site of a singing or cooking contest is also called 대회장.

en: gaps; the spaces here and there between things

examples.en: I tucked sticky notes in between the pages of the book.
I stretch for a moment in between bouts of work.
Sunlight comes in through the gaps between the trees.
The wind feels cool when I walk between the buildings.
I put a comma between every pair of sentences.

examples.ko: 연습 사이사이의 짧은 휴식이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: The short breaks between practice sessions help.

explain: '사이'는 하나의 틈이고, '사이사이'는 여러 군데의 틈을 함께 말해요. 그래서 '나무 사이'는 두 나무의 중간이고, '나무 사이사이'는 나무들 곳곳의 빈 곳이에요. 시간에도 써서 일과 일 사이의 짧은 시간들을 가리켜요.
explain_en: 사이 is one gap, while 사이사이 refers to many gaps at once. 나무 사이 is the space between two trees, but 나무 사이사이 is the open spaces here and there among the trees. It also works for time, meaning the short moments between tasks.

examples.en: The waste collection area is behind the apartment building.
I gathered the trash and threw it away at the dump.

examples.ko: 동네 쓰레기장 냄새 때문에 창문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: I closed the window because of the smell from the neighborhood dump.
I heard a big dump opened next to the mountain.
This road leads to the dump.
Please keep the waste area clean.

explain: '쓰레기통'은 쓰레기를 담는 통이고, '쓰레기장'은 쓰레기를 모아 두거나 버리는 장소예요. 종류별로 나눠서 버리는 곳은 '분리수거장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A 쓰레기통 is a bin that holds trash, while a 쓰레기장 is a place where trash is gathered or dumped. A spot where recyclables are sorted by type is called a 분리수거장.

examples.ko: 급하다고 액셀을 너무 세게 밟지 마세요.
examples.en: Even if you are in a hurry, don't press the accelerator too hard.
In this car the accelerator is on the right.
Beginner drivers find it hard to control the accelerator.

examples.ko: 신호가 바뀌자 그가 액셀에서 발을 뗐어요.
examples.en: When the light changed, he took his foot off the accelerator.
The car stopped and I just kept pressing the accelerator.
You have to raise your speed with the accelerator on an uphill road.

explain: 자동차에서 속도를 올리는 페달은 '액셀', 속도를 줄이는 페달은 '브레이크'예요. '엑셀'은 컴퓨터 프로그램 이름으로 쓰는 말이라서 철자가 비슷해도 헷갈리면 안 돼요.
explain_en: In a car, the pedal that raises speed is the 액셀 and the pedal that slows you down is the 브레이크. 엑셀 is the spelling used for the computer program (Excel), so do not mix the two up even though they look similar.

examples.en: The ball rolled slowly toward the goal.
The goalkeeper defended the goal until the end.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 골문 앞에서 기회를 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: That player missed a chance right in front of the goal.
Before the match I checked whether the goal wobbled.

examples.ko: 상대 골문까지 달리는 데 오 초 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took five seconds to run to the opponent's goal.
A net hangs on the goal.

explain: '골대'는 기둥과 가로대로 된 틀을 가리킬 때가 많고, '골문'은 공이 들어가는 입구 쪽을 가리켜요. 축구, 하키 같은 경기에서 써요.
explain_en: 골대 often points to the frame made of posts and a crossbar, while 골문 points to the opening the ball goes into. Both are used in sports like soccer and hockey.

examples.en: Let's meet in front of the school's south gate.
If you go out through the south gate, the subway station is close.
The south gate was closed, so I went around to the main gate.
There is a small flower shop at the park's south gate.

examples.ko: 남문에서 북문까지 걸어서 십 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about ten minutes on foot from the south gate to the north gate.
The taxi came in slowly past the south gate.

explain: '동문, 서문, 북문'과 짝을 이루는 말이에요. 큰 학교나 공원, 옛 성에서 출입구를 방향으로 나눠 부를 때 써요. '정문'은 방향이 아니라 중심이 되는 출입구를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It pairs with 동문, 서문 and 북문 (east, west, north gate). Large schools, parks and old fortresses name their entrances by direction this way. 정문 is not a direction; it is the main entrance.

en: do a thorough cleaning; give a place a big clean

examples.en: Every weekend the whole family gives the house a thorough clean.

examples.ko: 설날 전에 우리는 집 안을 대청소했어요.
examples.en: Before the New Year holiday we cleaned the whole house thoroughly.
We will give the classroom a thorough clean tomorrow afternoon.

examples.ko: 대청소하고 나니까 방이 두 배로 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: After the big clean, the room looks twice as big.

examples.ko: 다 같이 대청소하면 금방 끝날 거예요.
examples.en: If we all do the big clean together, it will be done quickly.
On the day of the big clean, we open all the windows.

explain: '청소하다'는 평소에 하는 청소이고, '대청소하다'는 구석구석까지 크게 하는 청소예요. 명절이나 이사처럼 큰 일을 앞두고 할 때가 있어요. '대청소를 하다'처럼 '대청소'를 명사로 써도 돼요.
explain_en: 청소하다 is everyday cleaning, while 대청소하다 is cleaning every corner on a big scale. People may do it before a holiday or a move. You can also use 대청소 as a noun, as in 대청소를 하다.

examples.en: We learned the recorder in music class.
The recorder has a clear, light sound.
My younger sibling plays an easy song on the recorder.
I don't know where my recorder is.
I took a recorder test when I was in elementary school.

examples.ko: 리코더에 입을 대고 천천히 불어 보세요.
examples.en: Put your mouth on the recorder and blow slowly.

explain: 리코더는 '불다'와 같이 써서 '리코더를 불다'라고 해요. 피아노는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'처럼 악기마다 짝이 되는 동사가 달라요. '리코더를 연주하다'라고도 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: You say 리코더를 불다 (literally, blow the recorder). Each instrument pairs with its own verb: 피아노를 치다 for the piano and 바이올린을 켜다 for the violin. You can also say 리코더를 연주하다.

examples.ko: 할머니는 길고양이를 불쌍히 여겨서 밥을 줬어요.
examples.en: Grandmother felt sorry for the stray cat and gave it food.

examples.ko: 힘든 사람을 불쌍히 여기는 마음은 누구에게나 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has a heart that feels pity for people who are struggling.

examples.ko: 저를 불쌍히 여기지 마세요, 저는 괜찮아요.
examples.en: Please don't pity me, I'm fine.

examples.ko: 부디 이 아이들을 불쌍히 여겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please take pity on these children.

examples.ko: 모두가 그 사정을 듣고 그를 불쌍히 여겼어요.
examples.en: Everyone heard his situation and felt sorry for him.

examples.ko: 남을 불쌍히 여길 줄 아는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a person who knows how to feel pity for others.

explain: '불쌍히 여기다'처럼 거의 '여기다'와 같이 써요. 다른 동사 앞에서는 보통 '불쌍하게'를 써서 '불쌍하게 울다'라고 해요. 상대에게 동정하는 마음이 담겨서, 듣는 사람이 기분 나빠할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used almost only with '여기다', as in '불쌍히 여기다'. Before other verbs people usually say '불쌍하게', as in '불쌍하게 울다'. It carries a feeling of pity toward someone, which can make the listener uncomfortable.

examples.en: My older sister is a stage actor.
To become a stage actor you need to practice your voice.
I met that stage actor and got an autograph.
Stage actors practice the same lines every day.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 연극배우로 살고 싶었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little I wanted to live as a stage actor.

examples.ko: 유명한 연극배우의 공연을 보러 극장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the theater to see a famous stage actor's performance.

explain: '배우'는 영화, 무대 등에서 연기하는 사람 모두를 가리키고, '연극배우'는 그중 무대에서 연기하는 사람이에요. '영화배우', '뮤지컬배우'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 어디서 연기하는지 구분해요.
explain_en: 배우 covers anyone who acts in film, on stage and so on, and 연극배우 is the one who acts on stage. Adding a word in front, as in 영화배우 or 뮤지컬배우, tells you where the person performs.

examples.en: The theme song of this movie is so good.
When I hear the theme song, I think of that drama.
Who sang the Olympic theme song?
I memorized the theme song lyrics and sang along.
My friend changed the ringtone to a cartoon's theme song.

examples.ko: 드라마 주제곡의 첫 소절만 들어도 알아요.
examples.en: I can tell from just the first line of the drama's theme song.

explain: '주제가'는 가사가 있는 노래를 가리키고, '주제곡'은 가사 없는 연주곡까지 넓게 가리킬 수 있어요. 영화, 드라마, 만화, 게임처럼 작품마다 대표 음악이 있을 때 써요.
explain_en: 주제가 points to a song with lyrics, while 주제곡 can also cover instrumental pieces without lyrics. You use it when a work such as a movie, drama, cartoon or game has a signature piece of music.

examples.en: I put the papers into a binder and organized them.
The binder is thick, so it doesn't fit in my bag.
I went to the stationery store to buy a new binder.

examples.ko: 수업 자료는 파란 바인더 안에 있어요.
examples.en: The class materials are in the blue binder.
If you bind them in a binder, the papers won't scatter.
The teacher said we need a binder.

explain: '파일'은 얇은 서류 보관 케이스를 가리킬 때 쓰고, '바인더'는 고리가 있어서 구멍 뚫은 종이를 끼워 두는 두꺼운 것을 가리킬 때 써요. 학교나 회사에서 자료를 모을 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: 파일 is used for a thin case that holds papers, while 바인더 is the thicker one with rings where you clip hole-punched paper. People use it to collect materials at school or work.

examples.en: New Zealand is an island country.
An island nation is surrounded by the sea.

examples.ko: 저는 작은 섬나라로 여행을 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to travel to a small island country.
In this island country people often eat fish.
Britain is also an island nation, and the weather is often cloudy.
Korea is not an island country; it is on a peninsula.

explain: '섬나라'는 한 단어라서 띄어 쓰지 않아요. 영국이나 뉴질랜드처럼 섬으로 이루어진 나라를 이렇게 불러요. 한국은 대륙에 이어진 '반도'에 있는 나라라서 섬나라가 아니에요.
explain_en: 섬나라 is one word, so you do not put a space in it. Countries made of islands, like Britain or New Zealand, are called this. Korea sits on a 반도 (peninsula) connected to the continent, so it is not a 섬나라.

examples.en: You have to wear work clothes at a construction site.
Work clothes should be sturdy and comfortable.
There is oil on my father's work clothes.
When I get to work I change into my work clothes first.
My work clothes were worn out, so I ordered new ones.
The company gave me two sets of work clothes.

explain: '교복'은 학교에서, '작업복'은 일터에서 입는 옷이에요. 옷 한 벌을 셀 때 '벌'을 써서 '작업복 한 벌'이라고 해요. 회사에서 맞춰 주는 옷은 '근무복'이나 '유니폼'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A 교복 is worn at school and a 작업복 is worn at the workplace. To count outfits you use the counter 벌, as in 작업복 한 벌. Clothes a company provides may also be called 근무복 or 유니폼.

en: wardrobe; large closet for clothes and bedding

examples.en: I put the blanket away in the wardrobe.

examples.ko: 장롱이 너무 커서 방이 좁아 보여요.
examples.en: The wardrobe is so big that the room looks small.
Moving the wardrobe was hard when we moved house.
Grandmother's room also has an old wardrobe.

examples.ko: 옷을 장롱에 걸어 두면 구겨지지 않아요.
examples.en: If you hang clothes in the wardrobe, they won't wrinkle.

examples.ko: 장롱은 보통 방 한쪽 벽에 놓아요.
examples.en: A wardrobe is usually placed against one wall of the room.

explain: '옷장'은 옷을 넣는 가구이고, '장롱'은 옷뿐 아니라 이불 같은 것도 넣어 두는 크고 튼튼한 가구예요. 옷 넣는 용도를 말하고 싶으면 '옷장'이라고 하면 돼요.
explain_en: 옷장 is furniture for clothes, while 장롱 is a large, sturdy piece of furniture that holds bedding such as blankets as well as clothes. If you want to stress that it is for clothes, you can say 옷장.

examples.en: I can see children picking grapes in the vineyard.
Grandfather runs a small vineyard.
The vineyard stretched out endlessly.
In autumn we go on a field trip to the vineyard.
There is a small road beside the vineyard.
This village's vineyards are very famous.

explain: 작물 이름 뒤에 '밭'을 붙여 '배추밭', '고구마밭', '포도밭'처럼 말해요. 쌀을 기르는 곳은 '밭'이 아니라 '논'이에요. 과일나무를 키우는 곳은 '과수원'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: You add 밭 after the crop name, as in 배추밭, 고구마밭 and 포도밭. The place where rice grows is not a 밭 but a 논. A place that grows fruit trees can also be called a 과수원.

examples.en: When you reach the upper grades of elementary school, the homework increases.
The older girls from the upper grades helped us.
This book is for the upper grades.
The lower grades and the upper grades have different break times.
My younger sibling will soon move up to the upper grades.
It is a slightly difficult problem for the upper grades.

explain: 반대말은 '저학년'이에요. 초등학교에서는 보통 1~2학년을 저학년, 3~4학년을 중학년, 5~6학년을 고학년이라고 불러요. 한 학년이 아니라 여러 학년을 묶어서 가리키는 말이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is 저학년 (lower grades). In elementary school, grades 1-2 are usually 저학년, grades 3-4 are 중학년 and grades 5-6 are 고학년. It groups several grades together rather than naming a single one.

examples.en: I played rugby with my friends on the weekend.
Rugby has a lot of physical contact, so you have to be careful.
I wonder how rugby differs from soccer.
I like soccer and I like rugby too.
My younger sibling got into university through rugby.
My dad was a rugby player when he was a student.

explain: '축구'는 발로 공을 차는 경기이고, '럭비'는 손으로 공을 들고 달릴 수 있는 경기예요. 공 모양도 달라서 럭비공은 둥글지 않고 길쭉해요.
explain_en: In 축구 (soccer) you kick the ball, while in 럭비 you may carry the ball in your hands and run. The ball differs too: a rugby ball is long and oval, not round.

examples.en: In summer I wear an anklet and sandals.
The anklet was pretty, so I bought one more.
An anklet is less noticeable than a bracelet.
I also bought an anklet that matches my friend's.
I tried adding some style with a small anklet.
The anklet strap broke, so I bought a new one.

explain: '팔찌'는 손목에, '발찌'는 발목에 차요. 뉴스에 나오는 '전자발찌'는 위치를 확인하는 장치라서 장신구와는 쓰임이 아주 달라요.
explain_en: A 팔찌 goes on the wrist and a 발찌 goes on the ankle. The 전자발찌 you hear about in the news is a device that tracks location, so it is very different from jewelry.

examples.en: There are one hundred new students this year in total.
The new students are gathered in the auditorium.
The seniors welcomed the new students.
They hand out new textbooks to the entering students.
I was also an entering student at this school last year.
The representative of the new students greeted everyone at the front.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '신입생'이 있어요. 짝이 되는 말은 학교를 마친 '졸업생'이에요.
explain_en: A similar word is 신입생. The counterpart is 졸업생, a student who has finished school.

examples.en: Our youngest is the well-known prankster of the family.

examples.ko: 장난꾸러기 동생 때문에 하루도 조용하지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of my mischievous younger sibling, no day is quiet.

examples.ko: 그 장난꾸러기가 또 선생님을 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: That prankster surprised the teacher again.
They say a prankster still loves playing jokes after growing up.
Many people call me a prankster.

examples.ko: 장난꾸러기에게는 혼내기보다 일을 맡기는 게 좋대요.
examples.en: They say it's better to give a prankster a task than to scold them.

explain: '-꾸러기'는 그런 모습이 많은 사람 뒤에 붙는 말이에요. '잠꾸러기', '욕심꾸러기', '심술꾸러기'처럼 쓰고, 보통 귀엽게 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 어린아이에게 많이 써요.
explain_en: The ending -꾸러기 attaches to a person who shows a lot of that trait. It appears in 잠꾸러기, 욕심꾸러기 and 심술꾸러기, and it usually has a cute, teasing feel. It is used mostly for young children.
